tfn.s: Fifteen restaurants have agreed to take part in the trial.
tfn.why: The text says: “Fifteen restaurants have agreed to take part in a one-month trial”.

tfn.s: Every restaurant on the island must follow the rule.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: “The restaurants chose to join the scheme, so it is not a rule for every restaurant on the island.”

tfn.s: The reunion kit contains games and drawings.
tfn.why: The text says: “It contains games and drawings designed to help children and parents spend time together.”

tfn.s: Most families in Sardinia like the idea.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text describes the trial but never says what most families think of it.

tfn.s: Parents can read about the risks of too much time online in the kit.
tfn.why: The text says the kit holds a leaflet that “explains the risks of too much time online”.

focus.note: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word, like put away. The small word changes the meaning, so learn them together.

tfn.s: The reunion kit includes information for parents as well as activities for children.
tfn.why: The kit has games and drawings, and also “a leaflet about the risks of too much screen time”.

tfn.s: Cau believes parents should deal with children's screen use alone.
tfn.why: The text says she “argues that the burden should not fall entirely on parents”.

tfn.s: The local association forced the restaurants to join the pilot.
tfn.why: The restaurants “volunteered”, and the association's president said they “had readily agreed”.

tfn.s: Families will have to pay extra for the reunion kit.
tfn.why: The text never mentions the price of the kit.

tfn.s: The scheme covers only some of the restaurants in Sardinia.

focus.note: Many phrasal verbs have a particle that adds a clear idea: away means removed, together means joined, on and with link the verb to an object.

tfn.s: The scheme could reach more restaurants only if the first month goes well, and only by choice.
tfn.why: Frongia plans “to extend it to other restaurants, voluntarily, if the month goes well”.

tfn.s: The writer sees a screen-free table as unlike anything restaurants normally ask of customers.
tfn.why: Restaurants “already set rules about reservations, menus and behaviour”, so it is “not an entirely new kind of condition”.

tfn.s: The writer suggests the pilot is worthwhile whatever its results turn out to be.
tfn.why: Nothing is yet known about whether it improves anything, yet “its value lies in the experiment itself”.

tfn.s: The games in the reunion kit were tested on children before the pilot began.
tfn.why: The text says they were designed with paediatricians but never mentions testing.

tfn.s: Cau holds that parents alone should be responsible for children's screen use.
tfn.why: She argues it “should not be treated as a task for parents alone”.

speak.title: Role-play: a phone-free table
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your restaurant has joined the phone-free trial. A family has just sat down. Explain the rule and the reunion kit. Answer the parent's worries and decide if there can be any exceptions.

b.text: You are eating out with two children and you are expecting an important message. You don't like being told what to do. Ask questions, explain your problem and try to agree a solution.

phrases: Could I just explain how it works?
It's only for one meal, and we've got games for the children.
I'd rather decide that for myself.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you reach an agreement, and was the rule fair?
